content: A diff refers to the comparison between two versions of a page, highlighting the differences between them. This feature can be accessed through the page history, where each version is accompanied by two radio buttons. The left button is used to select the older version, while the right button is for the newer version. By selecting these and pressing Compare selected versions, the differences between the two versions are displayed. In specific cases, such as comparing a single edit or the current version with an older one, you can use the cur or last links in the page history or the Recent Changes page. Additionally, during an edit conflict, the diff is shown to help you identify the exact changes that need to be reintegrated. Starting from MediaWiki version 1.5, the diff functionality is also available in preview mode, allowing you to compare the stored version with the current version in the edit box. When viewing a diff, the two versions are displayed side-by-side. In left-to-right languages, the older version appears on the left, while in right-to-left scripts, this arrangement is reversed. Paragraphs that differ are highlighted: yellow for the old version and green for the new version. Text removed within a paragraph is marked in red in the old version, while new text is marked in red in the new version. If an entire paragraph is added or removed, the text appears in black, and the corresponding side is left blank. Unchanged text is displayed in black on a grey background, with only the sections before and after the changes shown. The diff operates on a per-line basis, and some editors find that manually adding line breaks can improve the clarity of the diff. The diff page also includes links to the user pages and talk pages of the editors who made the last and current edits. Links to their contribution lists are also provided. For administrators (sysops), a rollback button is available, allowing them to revert the page to the older version. However, this button is displayed even when viewing a diff between a recent version and an older version that is not the immediate predecessor. In such cases, using the rollback button may undo changes that are not directly related to the displayed diff. For example, if User A vandalized a page and User B partially reverted the vandalism, the diff would show the remaining vandalism. However, rolling back would undo User B's partial repair rather than the vandalism itself. Edit summaries are displayed on the diff page, appearing in a row beneath the usernames. If the editor included links in their edit summary, these links remain functional on the diff page. In MediaWiki version 1.4, additional links to both versions, as well as the previous and next diffs, are provided. When moving or copying text within a page or from another page while making other edits, it is recommended to separate these edits. After the table of differences, the newer of the two compared versions is displayed in full. In the Classic skin with a quickbar, the diff page omits the quickbar to maximize the available space, making it useful for viewing the page in full-screen width without altering user preferences. In the Monobook skin, the panels on the left remain visible on the diff page. The diff page is more likely to widen due to the presence of two columns and the display of long URLs, which are not hidden. To compare two versions of a page using a URL, you can construct the URL manually. First, open the revision of one page you wish to compare, noting its oldid number (e.g., `&oldid=78722`). Then, open the revision of the other page and copy its oldid number. Replace the oldid parameter in the URL of the first page with diff (e.g., `&diff=78722`) and paste this string into the URL of the second page, placing it between the page's title and its oldid (e.g., `&oldid=98420`). The resulting URL will compare the two specified versions. If you wish to compare the current version of a page with a specific oldid, you can use current in place of the oldid after diff= (e.g., `Diff&diff=current&oldid=124558`). This will display the differences between the current version and the specified older version.
